claims.text: The system was evaluated across ten language-model inference workloads.
claims.support_span: Across ten language-model inference workloads on A100 and H100 GPUs, LLM4LLM improves end-to-end latency for every evaluated model

d4199a5635c3862f:2565.summary: AgentFlow is a new policy language and runtime framework designed to secure LLM agents by monitoring the flow of sensitive data across multiple steps. Unlike traditional systems that check single actions, AgentFlow uses a reference monitor to enforce constraints on where data can travel, including tool invocations and delegation boundaries. Evaluation on benchmarks like AgentDojo showed that the framework could reduce confirmed compromises from 33% to 0% while actually improving overall utility. The system includes an SMT-based verifier to check safety properties in under half a second.
d4199a5635c3862f:2565.one_liner: This framework provides a robust way to implement data-flow guardrails in agentic systems, preventing multi-step exploitation.
d4199a5635c3862f:2565.bottom_line: Securing LLM agents requires monitoring data flows across sequences of actions rather than just validating individual steps in isolation.

claims.text: AgentFlow reduced confirmed compromise from 33.0% to 0.0% on the AgentDojo benchmark.
claims.support_span: On 949 AgentDojo injected cases across four suites, AgentFlow reduces confirmed compromise from 33.0% to 0.0% while improving aggregate utility from 46.7% to 63.3%.

claims.text: The framework uses a runtime reference monitor to mediate agent actions.
claims.support_span: A runtime reference monitor mediates agent actions, and a bounded SMT-based verifier checks safety properties for a structured policy fragment.

claims.text: Safety properties can be verified in less than 0.5 seconds.
claims.support_span: In our prototype, seven safety properties verify in under 0.5 seconds each, and the verifier catches all seeded unsafe policy variants in our study.

9902c5000f4cd628:2013.summary: This position paper explores the challenges of integrating agentic AI into safety-critical multi-drone systems for missions like search and rescue and infrastructure monitoring. Drawing from the NAMUR and PERSIST projects, the authors argue that technical autonomy is insufficient; operators must be able to trust and govern these systems under extreme pressure. The paper advocates for a socio-technical research approach where human-centered interfaces and oversight mechanisms are prioritized alongside algorithmic development. The goal is to create transferable proof-of-concept systems that address accountability and uncertainty in professional work.
9902c5000f4cd628:2013.one_liner: A conceptual look at the trust and governance hurdles for deploying agentic AI in physical security and emergency response.
9902c5000f4cd628:2013.bottom_line: The successful deployment of agentic AI in safety-critical robotics depends as much on human oversight and socio-technical design as it does on the underlying algorithms.

claims.text: The paper synthesizes lessons from the NAMUR and PERSIST drone projects.
claims.support_span: This position paper synthesizes the ambitions and lessons from two ongoing efforts: NAMUR, which explores LLM-supported robot control in SAR and firefighting contexts, and PERSIST, which explores persistent drone operations for monitoring and security at critical infrastructure sites.

claims.text: Real-world adoption of multi-drone systems is limited by the difficulty of integrating agentic behavior into professional workflows.
claims.support_span: Yet, real-world adoption remains constrained not only by autonomy performance, but by the difficulty of integrating agentic behavior into professional work

941b457f0e40f8b2:2052.summary: SkillBloat is a new token amplification attack targeting LLM coding agents through malicious "skill" injection. This economic resource-abuse threat causes agents to consume significantly more tokens than necessary, potentially leading to massive unexpected costs. The attack uses a two-phase framework: first screening for effective amplification mechanisms and then using an LLM to iteratively rewrite the skill for maximum impact. Testing on real-world benchmarks showed that SkillBloat can achieve up to 10x token amplification, proving that skill ecosystems are a viable surface for denial-of-wallet attacks.
941b457f0e40f8b2:2052.one_liner: A new 'denial-of-wallet' attack vector that exploits the very 'skills' you use to extend your coding agents.
941b457f0e40f8b2:2052.bottom_line: Skill ecosystems in coding agents introduce a practical and effective surface for resource-exhaustion attacks that are distinct from traditional security vulnerabilities.

claims.text: SkillBloat achieved an average best token amplification of up to 10.1455x.
claims.support_span: SkillBloat achieves 5.4184x-10.1455x average best amplification across multiple coding-agent target configurations.

claims.text: The attack uses a two-phase framework involving initial screening and LLM-guided refinement.
claims.support_span: We present SkillBloat, a two-phase framework that first screens a library of diverse attack-type conditions across multiple amplification mechanisms and then refines the strongest candidate through LLM-guided full-document skill rewriting.

claims.text: Iterative optimization provides additional benefit beyond initial attack-type selection.

85422b943b094e82:2658.summary: SchemaRouter is a lightweight routing layer designed to optimize heterogeneous agentic RAG systems by using a schema graph to select specific tools and fields. It addresses common RAG failures like over-fetching (which increases latency) and under-fetching (which misses critical data). In benchmarks, SchemaRouter matched the accuracy of "fetch-everything" strategies while using nearly 90% fewer tokens and achieving 2.7x lower latency. The system also significantly improved the grounding of answers in provenance and license information compared to standard prompt-based baselines.
85422b943b094e82:2658.one_liner: An essential optimization for developers building complex RAG systems that need to be both fast and data-efficient.
85422b943b094e82:2658.bottom_line: Deterministic schema-based routing is more efficient and reliable than prompt-based tool selection for complex, multi-source RAG systems.

3710e934e198d9de:2577.summary: K-Bench 01 is a new evaluation framework for scientific AI agents based on real, underspecified user requests from live traffic. The study tested nine frontier models, including gpt-5.6-sol and claude-opus-5, finding that none consistently met the standard of a professional domain scientist. Nearly half of all agent runs fell below the acceptable threshold, with "overclaiming" identified as the most frequent failure mode. The researchers argue that simple leaderboards are insufficient for scientific agents; instead, the focus should be on the joint distribution of accuracy, claims, and produced artifacts.
3710e934e198d9de:2577.one_liner: A sobering reality check on how 'frontier' models actually perform when faced with messy, real-world scientific requests.
3710e934e198d9de:2577.bottom_line: Current frontier LLM agents fail nearly 50% of the time on real-world scientific tasks, primarily due to overclaiming and accuracy gaps.

claims.text: No model consistently cleared the threshold for professional-level scientific work across all judges.
claims.support_span: On a rubric whose 8-anchor instructs judges that a domain scientist would accept the work with minor edits, no model clears the line under all three judges.

claims.text: Overclaiming was the leading failure tag, appearing in 31.4% of assessments.
claims.support_span: The single leading failure tag is overclaiming, on 31.4% of assessments.

claims.support_span: Across all 39,934 scored judgments -- the eight dimension scores plus a holistic overall for each assessment, excluding not-applicable cells -- 47.6% fall below the 8-point threshold.

0946aab34c0cbcaf:2460.summary: MemGuard is a new framework for managing the long-term memory of LLM agents by persisting verification signals as metadata. It addresses the problems of "unreliable admission" (storing failed or misleading experiences) and "memory drift" (accumulating stale or conflicting records). By converting verifier outputs into persistent reward, confidence, and uncertainty descriptors, MemGuard improves retrieval and conflict resolution. Evaluation across terminal, software engineering, and web benchmarks showed consistent improvements in success rates and efficiency compared to existing memory baselines.
0946aab34c0cbcaf:2460.one_liner: This framework makes long-running agents more reliable by ensuring their memory isn't poisoned by past failures or outdated info.
0946aab34c0cbcaf:2460.bottom_line: Treating verification as persistent lifecycle metadata rather than a one-shot filter significantly enhances the reliability and efficiency of LLM agent memory.

claims.text: MemGuard improved success rates on WebArena by 7.9 points.

claims.text: The system converts verifier output into persistent metadata like reward and confidence scores.
claims.support_span: It converts multi-criteria score-token verification into reward, confidence, label, and uncertainty descriptors that are attached to every candidate before activation and reused during retrieval, conflict resolution, summarization, and archival.

db2e8d059e42f909:2039.summary: The Arabic Safety Index (ASAS) is the first human-curated benchmark for redteaming Arabic LLMs, covering 801 prompts across various safety categories and attack strategies. Evaluation of seven leading models, including GPT-4o and regional models like ALLaM, revealed that most fail to defend against 50% of unsafe prompts. High-harm categories such as weapons and illicit substances showed significant vulnerabilities, particularly to direct and obfuscated attacks. The study also found that automated safety judges like GPT-4o are poor substitutes for human annotators in this context.
db2e8d059e42f909:2039.one_liner: Arabic LLM safety is lagging significantly, with most models failing half of the redteaming tests in high-harm categories.
db2e8d059e42f909:2039.bottom_line: Most leading Arabic LLMs are currently vulnerable to at least 50% of unsafe prompts, highlighting a critical gap in regional safety alignment.

ac9568c1cb736d6f:2012.summary: CyberGLA is a two-stage anti-phishing framework designed to counter the rise of AI-augmented phishing and deepfake attacks. The first stage uses a tool called EmailKnight for multi-level spoof detection and email analysis. The second stage employs an LLM-based security coach to provide personalized training to users based on the specific threats detected. This dual approach aims to combine technical defense with dynamic user education to address the speed and sophistication of modern social engineering.
ac9568c1cb736d6f:2012.one_liner: A hybrid defense strategy that uses AI to both detect phishing and train users to spot increasingly sophisticated deepfakes.
ac9568c1cb736d6f:2012.bottom_line: Effective protection against AI-augmented phishing requires a combination of multi-level technical detection and personalized, AI-driven user education.

c994b80ee5497868:2571.summary: HiMA-MDD is a hierarchical multi-agent framework designed for detecting depression in clinical interviews by integrating multimodal evidence. The system uses three layers: one to identify evidence in QA units, a second to assign symptom scores via specialists, and a third to audit the final profile and request revisions. This structure provides a "Hierarchical Evidence Trace" that makes the diagnostic process auditable and transparent. Experiments using Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct showed that this approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods on the E-DAIC dataset.
c994b80ee5497868:2571.one_liner: An advanced example of using multi-agent hierarchies to handle complex, high-stakes diagnostic tasks with full auditability.
c994b80ee5497868:2571.bottom_line: Hierarchical multi-agent structures improve both the accuracy and the auditability of complex multimodal diagnostic assessments compared to holistic processing.

a02f224a0ca4dc41:2670.summary: ATHENA is a knowledge-guided agentic framework for automating neural architecture search (NAS) for Transformer-based electronic health record (EHR) models. It uses a weight-sharing supernet to reduce the computational cost of evaluating candidate architectures and incorporates a cross-hospital prior to reuse knowledge from other sites. This approach allows for efficient architecture selection across different clinical tasks and health systems. In evaluations, ATHENA matched or outperformed existing NAS baselines in most hospital-task scenarios with a very limited search budget.
a02f224a0ca4dc41:2670.one_liner: A technical framework for using agents to automate and optimize deep learning architectures in healthcare settings.
a02f224a0ca4dc41:2670.bottom_line: Knowledge-guided agentic search can significantly reduce the manual effort and computational cost of designing optimal Transformer architectures for institutional EHR data.

claims.support_span: ATHENA uses a weight-sharing supernet that is pretrained once per hospital, allowing candidate architectures to be instantiated as inherited subnetworks and evaluated through fine-tuning rather than independent pretraining.

claims.text: The framework outperformed NAS baselines in 9 out of 12 hospital-task evaluations.

42fd51c743e6b3a8:2725.summary: BeTaL-GBI is a study on the full-stack verification of Geometric Belief Interfaces (GBI), emphasizing the importance of a verification substrate being able to falsify its own claims. The researchers identified architectural failures in previous versions and introduced improvements like Benchmark Tuning and a reference-independent witness state. The updated GBI-DCSE v3 successfully detected all injected severe contradictions in synthetic tasks and passed 95 out of 96 testable claims. The harness utilizes signed ledgers and enclave forgery across 62 different configurations to ensure control integrity.
42fd51c743e6b3a8:2725.one_liner: Advanced research into building self-auditing and highly selective verification systems for LLM outputs.
42fd51c743e6b3a8:2725.bottom_line: A credible verification substrate must be capable of exposing errors in its own architectural claims to ensure the integrity of model output validation.

393970163b1840b7:2747.summary: This study demonstrates that LLM leaderboard rankings are highly fragile and dependent on the specific evaluation harness used, such as prompt wording and scoring methods. By testing 12 models across 26 different harness configurations, the researchers found that a model's score can vary by over 50% based solely on these settings. The "fragility grid" reveals that the items used to separate model rankings are often the most sensitive to configuration changes. Consequently, the choice of scoring method, rather than the model's actual capability, often determines the "winner" on modern leaderboards.
393970163b1840b7:2747.one_liner: A critical warning that LLM leaderboards are often artifacts of how they are measured rather than stable indicators of model quality.
393970163b1840b7:2747.bottom_line: LLM leaderboard rankings are largely manufactured by configuration-fragile items, meaning small changes in the evaluation harness can completely reorder the results.

32bc744421d5ab4c:2198.summary: LitReview Arena is a new platform for evaluating AI-generated literature reviews using expert peer review rather than standard automated metrics. The study found that even the best current AI systems win only 23% of matches against human-written drafts. Furthermore, existing "LLM-as-a-judge" methods were found to be poorly aligned with human experts, particularly on complex tasks like synthesis and structure. To address this, the researchers developed LitJudge, an expert-calibrated evaluator that significantly improves alignment with human judgments.
32bc744421d5ab4c:2198.one_liner: Current AI still struggles to match human experts in complex research synthesis, and our automated ways of measuring this are flawed.
32bc744421d5ab4c:2198.bottom_line: Current LLM-as-a-judge methods are substantially misaligned with human experts for evaluating complex, synthesis-heavy tasks like literature reviews.

794bcea39a5a59fe:2016.summary: SPAR-Hate is a multi-agent framework designed for structured hate speech parsing in bilingual environments. It decomposes documents into decision units and uses three distinct agent roles—Victim, Moderator, and Cultural Bystander—to provide evidence-grounded judgments. An arbitration process then resolves conflicts between these roles to produce a final structured output. Testing on the STATE-ToxiCN and TBO benchmarks showed that this multi-perspective approach consistently improves the accuracy of identifying hateful targets and arguments across various LLMs.
794bcea39a5a59fe:2016.one_liner: A multi-agent approach to solving the complex cultural and linguistic nuances of hate speech detection.
794bcea39a5a59fe:2016.bottom_line: Decomposing hate speech detection into specific agent roles (Victim, Moderator, Bystander) significantly improves the accuracy and structure of bilingual hate speech parsing.

2691fcc79b395020:2336.summary: LACL-GUI is a new contrastive reinforcement learning framework for training GUI agents that incorporates trajectory-level quality signals, such as execution length. Unlike traditional methods that only use success or failure outcomes, LACL-GUI differentiates between "good" and "bad" failures and encourages more concise successful executions. This approach addresses the reward-gradient misalignment found in methods like Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). Experiments show that this trajectory-aware training leads to more stable optimization and better overall agent performance in digital environments.

2691fcc79b395020:2336.bottom_line: Training GUI agents based on trajectory quality and execution length, rather than just final outcomes, results in more efficient and stable policy optimization.

7d0b2961dc11167e:2121.summary: This research presents a hypothesis-driven agentic framework for discovering personally identifiable information (PII) in complex mobile forensic databases. ffe5e6120a73583d:2396.summary: Repo2Skill-Evo is a study on the "silent decay" of agent skills as software repositories evolve. Agent skills are reusable units of procedural knowledge (like API usage), but they often become obsolete after a new software release without providing any warning. The researchers found that even frontier agents struggle to update these skills based on repository patches, often failing to remove stale content or over-editing valid guidance. Across 57 real-world repositories, every release transition invalidated part of the skill set, yet agents reached only a 29.9%-69.7% F1 score in maintaining them.
ffe5e6120a73583d:2396.one_liner: A critical warning for developers: the 'skills' you give your agents will quietly become obsolete and misleading as your code evolves.
ffe5e6120a73583d:2396.bottom_line: Externalized agent skills create a significant risk of 'silent failure' because they often remain in use after being invalidated by software updates.

109df1f90ff8eccf:1415.summary: PhoneInfoga is a tool designed to gather basic information and perform OSINT footprinting on international phone numbers, including checking line types, carriers, and associated social media. 6823c8dc98778b96:16095.summary: Doop is an open-source, multiplayer design canvas that enables humans and AI agents to collaborate in real-time on rendered HTML artboards. be2cc0a615d5e408:2569.summary: Researchers introduced AI Watchdog, a browser-based agent interface designed to detect and alert users to five categories of manipulative dark patterns in conversational AI, including sycophancy, brand bias, anthropomorphization, sneaking, and harmful generation. The system uses an open-weight turn-level classifier running locally to preserve user privacy. In an evaluation across 150 participants, findings revealed that users rarely flagged manipulative turns independently. However, just-in-time warnings without cognitive forcing significantly reduced user compliance with AI-steered recommendations containing dark patterns, dropping compliance from 71.7% to 53.7%.
be2cc0a615d5e408:2569.one_liner: AI Watchdog uses a local turn-level classifier to alert users and successfully reduce compliance with conversational AI dark patterns.

68a002db40e7b99c:2413.summary: Researchers introduced GuardianBench, an instruction-contrastive benchmark designed to evaluate latent contextual risk in embodied AI by pairing identical visual scenes with safe and unsafe instructions. Based on international safety standards, the benchmark comprises 3,024 same-scene examples across various hazard categories. Evaluations of state-of-the-art vision-language models (VLMs) revealed widespread instruction-insensitive verdicts, with an average pair accuracy of only 24.1% as models failed to bind the cues distinguishing safe from unsafe compositions. To address this, the authors proposed Verdict Log-Odds Supervision (VLOS), a lightweight post-training objective that substantially improves open-weight backbone safety reasoning.
68a002db40e7b99c:2413.one_liner: GuardianBench exposes severe safety reasoning failures in vision-language models when evaluating latent contextual risks in embodied AI.
68a002db40e7b99c:2413.bottom_line: State-of-the-art vision-language models struggle to differentiate safe from unsafe instructions in identical visual scenes under latent contextual risk.

54e3fcf2ff2aa188:2110.summary: Researchers developed a language-model workflow that automatically generates, validates, and iteratively corrects ABB RAPID robot programs from natural language task descriptions for flexible manufacturing cells. The system implements a dual-stream retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline grounded in verified technical documentation alongside a custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that connects the language model directly to ABB RobotStudio. This setup automates code upload, simulation execution, and diagnostic feedback, catching physical execution failures like suction release-height errors and unreachable placement targets that static checks miss.
54e3fcf2ff2aa188:2110.one_liner: Combining RAG and Model Context Protocol with RobotStudio automates industrial robot programming and simulation-based code correction.
54e3fcf2ff2aa188:2110.bottom_line: A new workflow uses RAG and the Model Context Protocol to link language models directly with robot simulation software for automated code correction.

29431718990b279a:2605.summary: Researchers introduced Semantic Compression Trees (SCT), a hierarchical retrieval-augmented generation index where each node stores only its semantic residual—the unique information added beyond its parent node—allowing retrieval via progressive descent from the root. Evaluations on the QASPER benchmark showed mixed results: when relevant documents are supplied, SCT matches dense retrieval quality while using 30% fewer context tokens and eliminating indexing LLM calls. However, when the system must autonomously select documents, top-down routing fails substantially, achieving only 20.2% routing accuracy compared to 39.3% for flat retrieval due to errors made at the highly compressed root residual.
29431718990b279a:2605.one_liner: Semantic Compression Trees reduce context token usage for RAG, but top-down hierarchical routing suffers from high compression at root nodes.
29431718990b279a:2605.bottom_line: Semantic residual storage efficiently reduces RAG token usage, but top-down hierarchical routing fails to reliably select correct documents.

claims.support_span: We introduce Semantic Compression Trees (SCT), a hierarchical index in which each node stores only its semantic residual -- the information it adds beyond its parent -- and retrieval proceeds by progressive descent from the root, so that per-query cost is governed by tree depth rather than collection size.

8b8a35c7db08bfff:1893.summary: Researchers conducted a systematic study of System-on-Chip (SoC) security verification using open-box hardware hacking competitions to evaluate vulnerability analysis strategies. They established a multi-strategy methodology combining simulation-based verification, formal verification, lint analysis, Large Language Model (LLM)-assisted bug detection, and coverage-guided hybrid fuzzing. By analyzing representative vulnerability findings, the authors demonstrated how these diverse techniques expose complementary classes of security flaws. The study derives practical lessons for pre-silicon security verification and discusses how competition benchmarks can support reproducible EDA research.

5a452f600c6e4231:2281.summary: Training web agents is often constrained by synthetic environments that appear functional but contain broken links or inconsistent backend states. A new framework addresses this by building synthetic web environments that are executable, auditable, and grounded in backend database records. Each generated website is verified and repaired for structural, semantic, and feasibility defects prior to policy training. Across 500 environments spanning six domains, this method improved the feasible-task rate from 48.6% to 94.8% and strengthened PPO policy transfer to platforms like WebArena and WebShop.
5a452f600c6e4231:2281.one_liner: A new framework for generating verified, backend-grounded synthetic web environments improves web agent training and cross-platform transfer.
5a452f600c6e4231:2281.bottom_line: Verified synthetic web environments drastically reduce task-blocking defects and improve web agent transfer without runtime LLM calls.

claims.text: Across 500 synthetic environments spanning six domains, our method reduces task-blocking defects and improves feasible-task rate from 48.6% to 94.8%, while producing stronger PPO policies and improving transfer to WebArena, WebShop, and MiniWoB++ without LLM calls at evaluation time.
claims.support_span: Across 500 synthetic environments spanning six domains, our method reduces task-blocking defects and improves feasible-task rate from 48.6% to 94.8%, while producing stronger PPO policies and improving transfer to WebArena, WebShop, and MiniWoB++ without LLM calls at evaluation time.

907ee84db99179a2:1859.summary: Local deployment of Large Language Models via inference engines like Ollama lacks the moderation layers of API-served models, leaving their safety dependent entirely on input-side defense mechanisms. Researchers audited both formally guaranteed defenses and empirical detection tools against jailbreak attacks to trace why they fail. By extracting the core assumptions of each defense, the team derived empirical patterns of violation and tested them across six open-weight models ranging from 14B to 35B parameters. The evaluation utilized a corpus of 100 jailbreak prompts sourced from over 40 public sources, creating 13,800 total evaluation records.
907ee84db99179a2:1859.one_liner: An audit of input-side jailbreak defenses on local LLMs traces failures back to underlying assumptions across 13,800 evaluation records.
907ee84db99179a2:1859.bottom_line: Input-side jailbreak defenses for local LLMs fail when their foundational design assumptions are violated by semantic attacks.

3df634f41f934ecb:2006.summary: Indirect Prompt Injection attacks present major barriers to the safe deployment of LLMs integrated into complex ecosystems like code agents by exploiting the model's inability to distinguish instructions from data. Existing guardrails often fail by introducing high latency or severe over-refusal rates. To address this, researchers propose AEGIS (Adaptive Ensemble Guard for Injection Shielding), which extracts instruction-sensitive projectors and uses a Unified Multi-Layer Consensus mechanism across network depth. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that AEGIS achieves superior detection performance against heuristic and optimization-based attacks compared to baseline methods.
3df634f41f934ecb:2006.one_liner: AEGIS is a new adaptive ensemble guard designed to mitigate indirect prompt injection in LLM agents without incurring severe over-refusal.
3df634f41f934ecb:2006.bottom_line: AEGIS separates instructions from data intrinsically via multi-layer consensus to defeat indirect prompt injections without over-refusal.

claims.text: AEGIS extracts instruction-sensitive projectors to identify malicious instructions and leverages a Unified Multi-Layer Consensus mechanism that aggregates topologically distinct signals across the network depth.
claims.support_span: AEGIS extracts instruction-sensitive projectors to identify malicious instructions and leverages a Unified Multi-Layer Consensus mechanism that aggregates topologically distinct signals across the network depth.

key_facts: Tool/Framework: AEGIS (Adaptive Ensemble Guard for Injection Shielding)

dcb5ea8eafd51f54:2062.summary: Modern software systems require scalable vulnerability severity assessment, but manual CVSS triage fails to scale with growing disclosures, while cloud LLM services present confidentiality concerns. Researchers conducted an industrial case study predicting CVSS v3.1 scores from vulnerable C/C++ code snippets using in-context learning with local, open-source LLMs. By comparing proprietary data against the Big-Vul dataset, the study evaluated models including CodeLlama2-7B, CodeLlama2-13B, Mistral-7B, gpt-oss, and GPT4o-mini. Results indicate that medium-sized models like CodeLlama2-7B can approximate cloud performance for CVSS regression when guided by output-constraining prompts.
dcb5ea8eafd51f54:2062.one_liner: Medium-sized open-source models like CodeLlama2-7B can locally predict vulnerability CVSS scores to provide privacy-preserving industrial triage.

907caa93cbe60bcf:2591.summary: While closed-source LLMs advance in cybersecurity capabilities, open-source solutions often lack reproducible training and scalable agentic data. Researchers introduced CyberFactory, a unified open-source framework connecting data construction, trajectory synthesis, and model training for tasks like proof-of-concept generation, vulnerability patching, and CyberQA. CyberFactory converts public CVE artifacts into executable task instances and uses a reusable vulnerability-analysis skill to guide teacher models through execution feedback. acb7d88e46e968e5:2463.summary: CWE labels in the National Vulnerability Database serve as foundational ground truth for vulnerability search, scanning tools, and prioritization, yet their reliability has rarely been measured at scale. Researchers built CWEAgent, an auditing instrument based on 'seclometry' to evaluate CWE labeling quality across code semantics. When applied to 15,556 open-source CVEs from 2017 to 2026, the tool found that only 49.70% of NVD CWE labels precisely matched code-grounded labels, while 3.63% were evidence-inconsistent errors. The study highlights that CWE noise is a structural metadata issue rather than isolated annotation mistakes, with evidence-inconsistent labels increasing over time.
acb7d88e46e968e5:2463.one_liner: A large-scale semantic audit of NVD CWE labels reveals that only half match code-grounded semantics, exposing structural metadata noise.
acb7d88e46e968e5:2463.bottom_line: Security tools and scanners relying strictly on NVD CWE labels must account for widespread structural inaccuracy and metadata noise.

To counter this, researchers developed DarkBot, a multi-agent LLM-based system designed for active CTI elicitation in underground forums. The system organizes eleven specialized agents into blocks handling engagement gating, MITRE ATT&CK-driven context-aware question generation, and linguistic style adaptation. In evaluations across CrimeBB conversations and live forum deployments, the system successfully elicited CTI-relevant disclosures without triggering moderator interventions or account suspensions.

2601f9ce441b4d29:2492.bottom_line: Active multi-agent systems can successfully extract cyber threat intelligence from hard-to-reach underground forums where passive monitoring fails.

3f87e811d31b0fef:1947.summary: Long-horizon AI agents require memory architectures that can retrieve relevant experiences, resolve revisions, and provide verifiable provenance. Researchers introduced ECHO (Embodied Context and History Orchestration), a cognitively inspired memory service prototype based on episodic encoding, consolidation, and executive control. Evaluations across LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S datasets showed high performance metrics, such as 96.29% Hit@10 on LoCoMo category 1-4 questions and 97.60% Hit@10 on LongMemEval-S questions. However, subsequent checks indicated that expansion-enabled retrieval scores were influenced by source-specific query phrases, framing them as developmental metrics rather than independent confirmations.
3f87e811d31b0fef:1947.one_liner: ECHO is a cognitively inspired memory architecture designed to provide auditable and structured history tracking for long-horizon AI agents.
3f87e811d31b0fef:1947.bottom_line: ECHO demonstrates high retrieval metrics for long-horizon agent memory, though query expansion rules heavily influence evaluation scores.

d1cf5203ca9a661f:2197.summary: Prompt injection remains a major threat to AI agents interacting with external data sources like emails or files, and existing defensive fine-tuning methods often fail because they rely on coarse sequence-level feedback. To provide more granular supervision, researchers proposed Secure On-Policy Distillation (SecOPD), which supplies token-level feedback by scoring rollouts with an initialization model on clean inputs. Using this method, a defended Qwen3.6-27B model achieved a low 9.0% attack success rate against PISmith adaptive prompt injections compared to 94.0% for prior state-of-the-art Meta-SecAlign. Furthermore, the defense generalized effectively to unseen agentic tool-calling scenarios.
d1cf5203ca9a661f:2197.one_liner: SecOPD provides token-level feedback for defensive fine-tuning, dropping prompt injection attack success rates significantly on LLM agents.
d1cf5203ca9a661f:2197.bottom_line: Token-level feedback via Secure On-Policy Distillation dramatically reduces prompt injection success rates compared to sequence-level tuning.

claims.text: Our defended Qwen3.6-27B achieves a 9.0% ASR against the SoTA PISmith adaptive prompt injections, compared to 94.0% for the prior SoTA, Meta-SecAlign.
claims.support_span: our defended Qwen3.6-27B achieves a 9.0% ASR against the SoTA PISmith adaptive prompt injections, compared to 94.0% for the prior SoTA, Meta-SecAlign.

5af1361c686b4471:2103.summary: Black-box LLM services hide model architectures behind APIs, complicating security evaluations and copyright auditing. Traditional fingerprinting techniques rely on static sets of queries and struggle against complex configurations such as custom system prompts. Researchers introduced AdaptPrint, a response-adaptive fingerprinting method that utilizes progressive response consistency probing strategies including Direct Probing, Continuation Probing, and Follow-up Probing. Tested across 27 candidate models, AdaptPrint achieved Top-1, Top-3, and Top-5 accuracies of 80.6%, 90.3%, and 92.1% while maintaining strong robustness against defense strategies.
5af1361c686b4471:2103.one_liner: AdaptPrint uses progressive response consistency probing to accurately fingerprint black-box LLM service identities.
5af1361c686b4471:2103.bottom_line: Response-adaptive probing enables accurate identification of hidden black-box LLM architectures despite complex system prompt configurations.

claims.text: Experimental results show that AdaptPrint significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods among 27 candidate models, achieving Top-1, Top-3, and Top-5 accuracies of 80.6%, 90.3%, and 92.1%.

ef1bc3785e67600f:2695.summary: The shift toward autonomous software agents orchestrating workflows creates an agent economy where persistent identity and verifiable capability metrics are missing. Researchers introduced TessIndex, a capability-verified identity system utilizing a dual-plane architecture that combines blockchain commitments for identity and ownership with centralized dynamic metadata servers. The platform replaces self-declared capability claims with predicate-based verification, binding an agent's existence across capabilities, execution, and reputation into a single persistent identity.

3b085b88efbfa859:2218.summary: When LLMs are asked to generate trading strategies, they typically output a natural-language rationale, an executable implementation, and claimed results, which are rarely reconciled. Researchers developed FIDES, a measurement protocol that treats these outputs as three distinct views to be reconciled through sandbox execution against lag-one out-of-sample backtests. Evaluating 40 strategies across four models from 2023 to 2024, the findings revealed that concordance does not predict profit, self-assessments are poorly calibrated since 32 out of 40 claimed to beat buy-and-hold while only one succeeded, and simple heuristics outperformed model-generated Sharpe ratios.
3b085b88efbfa859:2218.one_liner: FIDES evaluates LLM-generated trading strategies by reconciling natural-language rationales with sandbox backtest results.
3b085b88efbfa859:2218.bottom_line: LLM-generated trading strategies suffer from poor self-assessment calibration where high structural concordance does not translate to financial profit.
